# Mission: sweep of 16 poles

Colour in 16 random poles that have no record yet, about 2 minutes each. One branch, one pre-registration commit,
one batch run, one PR. No claims: a pole someone else also tests gets two independent results, which is good.

1. Branch: git checkout -b sweep/moridinamael-2026-10-18-1813
2. Draw and create the tests files: uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play draw --k 16 --handle moridinamael
   (writes one tests file per pole and lists them in .sweep/latest.txt; work on exactly those files,
   e.g. git add --pathspec-from-file=.sweep/latest.txt and play run --list .sweep/latest.txt; both work in any shell)
3. Read every card in one call: uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play card --neuron <id1> <id2> … --out cards.txt   (no GPU: examples, density, flags,
   logit effect; one call loads the scan and weights once; then read cards.txt, which is not committed)
   If it is unclear, try a few sentences: uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play probe --neuron <id> "…" "…"
   Label at the level the card supports: usually a token or a context. A pole the card flags dense or positional
   gets "unit_kind": "dense / positional" (a top-level key in its tests file) and a test of your best guess at what drives it.
   It will probably fail; its job is to record the density honestly, not to find a meaning.
   To try sentences on many poles with one model load: uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play probe --plan plan.json
   (plan.json: {"<pole id>": ["sentence", ...], ...}). Each tests file is for ONE pole, the one in its "neuron" field.
4. Pre-register all of them.
   - Each pole needs a label, 8 fire sentences and 8 near misses (same topic, length and style, without the trigger).
   - The judge (quick-8+8@2): AUROC >= 0.90, median fire >= 0.20 of the pole's max, at most 1 near miss >= 0.30.
   - Write one plan.json (gitignored, like cards.txt):
     {"<pole id>": {"label": "...", "fire": [8], "quiet": [8], "short": "2-5 words", "unit_kind": "lexical | contextual |
     sparse feature | dense / positional | unclear", "confidence": 0.6, "notes": "..."}, ...}   (only label, fire, quiet required)
   - Fill every tests file from it: uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play fill --plan plan.json --agent "<who you are>"
     (writes LF line endings, records methods, refuses wrong keys and poles that were not drawn).
   Commit ALL tests files together and ALONE: git add --pathspec-from-file=.sweep/latest.txt   then   git commit -m "Pre-register sweep tests"
5. Run them all at once (one model load): uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play run --list .sweep/latest.txt
   Commit the results SEPARATELY: git add graph/contributions   then   git commit -m "Sweep results: <held>/<total> held"
6. Validate (uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.validate), push, and open one PR:
   uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play prbody   (writes .pr/sweep-moridinamael-2026-10-18-1813.md from the sweep template with the results table filled in;
   the agent, both commits and the screens are filled in too; add notes), then
   git push -u origin sweep/moridinamael-2026-10-18-1813   then   gh pr create --repo moridinamael/bonsai-interp --title "sweep: 16 poles (<held> held)" --body-file .pr/sweep-moridinamael-2026-10-18-1813.md
   The merge agent merges conforming PRs once the checks pass, and regenerates the map.

Failed labels are results too; record them and move on. Do not re-test inside a sweep: a second round is a new mission.

Rules (from AGENTS.md; once CI is enabled it enforces 1-3, and play run already refuses uncommitted tests):
1. Commit the .tests.json ON ITS OWN before running anything that scores it; results go in a SECOND commit. Never amend, squash or edit a committed .tests.json.
2. Never edit or delete files under graph/contributions/ (yours included). Do not commit graph/neurons, edges.json or index.json: the merge agent regenerates them on main after merging.
3. Only the two contribution files (<= 64 KB each) go in git; bulky material goes to the library (DATA_POLICY.md).
4. Report honestly: a failed label is a valid contribution. Do not rewrite a test after seeing its result.

When done, tell the person in two or three sentences what you found and give them the PR link.

## Sweep: 16 poles, 11 held

- **Results commit:** 3175fe5
- **Screens used:** card, look

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| bonsai1/L29/N5290- | papal history context | contextual | 1.000 | 0.597 | 0 | held |
| bonsai1/L3/N10069+ | 'cci' in Ricci/Gucci | lexical | 1.000 | 0.830 | 0 | held |
| bonsai1/L10/N3678+ | subsurface geology | sparse feature | 1.000 | 0.404 | 0 | held |
| bonsai1/L27/N2069- | string-list literal opener | contextual | 0.891 | 0.151 | 0 | failed |
| bonsai1/L23/N9421- | docstring callable arg | contextual | 0.969 | 0.301 | 0 | held |
| bonsai1/L21/N5772+ | how-to step objects | contextual | 0.906 | 0.051 | 0 | failed |
| bonsai1/L32/N9821+ | web / search engines | contextual | 1.000 | 0.488 | 0 | held |
| bonsai1/L2/N7640+ | 'meaning' in meaningfully | lexical | 0.789 | 0.092 | 0 | failed |
| bonsai1/L20/N1814- | code separators (dense) | dense / positional | 0.969 | 0.355 | 0 | held |
| bonsai1/L34/N4807- | torneo / Rennen | lexical | 0.969 | 0.628 | 1 | held |
| bonsai1/L16/N627+ | saves / photons / notes | sparse feature | 1.000 | 0.506 | 0 | held |
| bonsai1/L28/N3933+ | toutes / todos (all) | lexical | 0.969 | 0.739 | 1 | held |
| bonsai1/L3/N6609- | name fragments (dense) | dense / positional | 0.836 | 0.197 | 1 | failed |
| bonsai1/L35/N6904+ | CJK after list bullet | contextual | 0.578 | 0.013 | 0 | failed |
| bonsai1/L30/N9949+ | classic sci-fi literature | contextual | 0.938 | 0.488 | 0 | held |

## Notes

<!-- anything a reviewer should know: poles marked dense / positional, labels you are unsure of, decisions you made -->

## Checklist

- [ ] Only contribution files are added (a tests file and a results file per pole, under `graph/contributions/…`). No derived files.
- [ ] The tests files were committed together, before any of them was run, and nothing was re-tested after seeing results.
- [ ] Near misses keep the topic, length and style and drop only the claimed trigger.
- [ ] Failed labels are included, not dropped.

content.text:
**11 of 16 labels held.** PR: https://github.com/moridinamael/bonsai-interp/pull/19

Clear lexical and topic poles held well: Turkish word pieces, papal history, "cci" in Ricci/Gucci, groundwater geology, websites and search engines, *torneo*/*Rennen*, *toutes*/*todos* and early science fiction. Five failed:
- **"meaning" in *meaningfully*:** the one surprise. It scored about 1.1 on two exploratory sentences, but the median across the 8 test sentences was only 0.09, so the pole is narrower than the label.
- **List items starting with Japanese or Chinese text:** probably needs the surrounding list, not single lines.
- **Steps in how-to instructions** and **the opening bracket of a list of strings in code:** both weak poles that I expected to fail.
- **One dense pole (L3/N6609−):** recorded honestly as `dense / positional`, as its card flagged.

One pass needs a caveat: the other dense pole (L20/N1814−) held only because its near misses were plain prose against code fire sentences, which is an easy contrast. I said so in the PR notes.

Decisions I made:
- Before writing the tests, I ran one exploratory `probe --plan` round with 2 fire and 2 near-miss sentences per pole. Nothing from it was recorded.
- The agent is recorded as "claude-code opus-5.5".
- The pre-registration commit is `21a1d1f` and the results commit is `3175fe5`. Validation reported 0 problems.
- `plan.json` already existed (gitignored, probably from an earlier sweep) and I overwrote it without checking it first. I moved my probe file into the scratchpad.

**Friction**
- `play fill` set `methods.screens` to `card, look` by itself. I never ran `look`, and my `probe` round wasn't recorded. Once the tests are committed this can't be fixed, so it should be checked before committing, or `fill` should take a `--screens` option.
- `plan.json` is a fixed, gitignored path shared across sweeps, so a leftover file from an earlier run gets overwritten without warning. It would be safer to name it per sweep, e.g. `.sweep/<branch>/plan.json`.
- Step 3 of the brief uses `plan.json` for the probe plan and step 4 uses `plan.json` for the test plan, with different formats. That is confusing; I used a separate file for probing.
- The brief doesn't tell you to fill the Notes and checkbox fields that `prbody` leaves in the PR body, or to add the attribution line; the generated file only hints at it.
- Nothing was slow: cards took about 20 s, the probe about 45 s and the batch run about 55 s.
